Working model illustrating the cellular, physiological, and biochemical mechanisms underlying polyploid stress resilience

A working model illustrating the cellular, physiological, and biochemical mechanisms underlying polyploid stress resilience.Molecules that show significant increases in polyploids are highlighted in red, whereas those that decrease in polyploids are highlighted in blue. The bottom left panel depicts reactive oxygen species (ROS) scavenging, gibberellin signaling, proline biosynthesis, and the SOS pathway in polyploids under stress. Plant stress induces the accumulation of ROS as potential signaling molecules; however, ROS can also damage membrane integrity and destabilize cellular compartments. Loss of cellular compartmentalization leads to ion leakage and physiological perturbations that affect plant growth and development. Redox signaling and antioxidant enzyme responses are schematized, as well as membrane destabilization resulting from lipid peroxidation. The bottom right panel illustrates abscisic acid (ABA) biosynthesis and the major ABA signaling pathway in polyploid plants under stress. In the presence of ABA, PYR/PYL/RCAR receptors bind ABA and engage with PP2Cs (negative regulators), releasing SnRK2 kinases (positive regulators). SnRK2s are activated through phosphorylation of their activation loop by Raf-like kinases or casein kinase 2. Once activated, SnRK2s can phosphorylate various downstream substrates, including transcription factors, ion channels, and enzymes, ultimately triggering ABA-responsive processes.
